skill.name: react-doctor
skill.description: Run React Doctor to assess React projects for security, performance, correctness, architecture, accessibility, bundle size, and dead code issues.
skill.summary: Audit React projects and prioritize actionable code health improvements.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: The eval finding is a false positive because SKILL.md only names eval as an issue that React Doctor detects. The documented npx command executes an unpinned latest package without confirmation, creating a supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: The usage command downloads and executes react-doctor@latest with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and remove -y so users can review installation before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - **Security**: hardcoded secrets in client bundle, eval()

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 lists eval() as a security issue that React Doctor detects. It does not instruct the agent or project to evaluate code.

Lines 13-15 direct execution of npx -y react-doctor@latest, which downloads and runs an unpinned package without confirmation. A compromised or changed latest release could execute arbitrary package lifecycle or CLI code.

content.value_statement: React projects can hide security, performance, correctness, and architecture problems. This skill runs React Doctor and guides prioritized fixes using reported diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Runs React Doctor from a React project root.
Reviews diagnostics with reported file paths and line numbers.
Covers security, performance, correctness, architecture, accessibility, and bundle concerns.
Re-runs the audit to verify score changes after fixes.
limitations: Requires a compatible React project and access to the React Doctor package.
Executes a third-party package through npx and should use a reviewed pinned version.
Diagnostic accuracy depends on React Doctor rules and project configuration.
A higher score does not replace tests, manual review, or production monitoring.

use_cases.description: Run a broad health audit and receive prioritized findings before a release.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pull request
use_cases.description: Identify correctness, performance, and architecture issues before requesting peer review.

use_cases.title: Assess inherited code
use_cases.description: Establish a baseline score and organize remediation work for an unfamiliar React project.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this React project with React Doctor. Summarize the score and list the highest-severity findings first.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a clear project health overview.

prompt_templates.title: Fix critical findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Run React Doctor, fix the reported errors, and explain each change. Re-run the audit and report the updated score.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants verified fixes for urgent diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project and prioritize performance and bundle findings. Recommend scoped changes and note expected tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is reducing rendering and bundle costs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a full remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased remediation plan from React Doctor diagnostics. Group related findings, estimate risk, apply safe fixes, and verify each phase.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical lead is improving a large codebase incrementally.

output_examples.input: Audit this React application and summarize the main problems.
output: Highest priority: missing server action authorization and effect cleanup.
Next steps: fix errors, address bundle imports, then re-run the audit.

output_examples.input: Fix the highest-severity React Doctor findings and verify the result.
output: Resolved the two reported errors in the referenced components.
The follow-up audit increased the score from 68 to 82.
Three lower-severity architecture findings remain for separate review.

best_practices: Run the audit from the project root with dependencies available.
Review each diagnostic in context before changing behavior.
Re-run tests and React Doctor after each focused group of fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the numeric score as proof of production readiness.
Do not apply every suggested change without reviewing project intent.
Do not execute an unreviewed latest package version in sensitive repositories.

faq.question: What does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It uses React Doctor diagnostics covering security, state, effects, architecture, performance, correctness, Next.js, bundles, accessibility, and dead code.

faq.question: Does it modify my project automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow asks the agent to review diagnostics and fix issues, so project files may change during remediation.

faq.question: How is the score interpreted?
faq.answer: Scores of 75 or higher are great, 50 to 74 need work, and 0 to 49 are critical.

faq.question: Can it audit Next.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented rules include metadata, server data fetching, async client components, server actions, and deferred server work.

faq.question: Does a passing score guarantee security?
faq.answer: No. The score reflects available rules and does not replace threat modeling, dependency review, testing, or manual security assessment.

faq.question: Why should the package version be pinned?
faq.answer: Pinning a reviewed version reduces unexpected changes and supply-chain exposure from automatically executing the latest published release.
